text:
Valerie Fiesser will never forget her surprise when Bukayo Saka contacted her out of the blue, asking whether he could help support a project in Nigeria in 2022. “I remember thinking: ‘Is this really Bukayo writing us an email?’” says the president of BigShoe, a non-profit organisation based in Frankfurt that has helped more than 10,000 children worldwide. “But that’s how he is. He’s always asking what more we can do.”
Four years on from that unexpected email, Fiesser was given the secret task of reaching out for a letter for Saka to read from the podium when he was presented with the Sócrates award at last month’s Ballon d’Or ceremony in London for his humanitarian work. She got the words from Byiringiro, a 14-year-old from Rwanda who had his eyesight restored after having surgery thanks to BigShoe’s initiative.
“They told me he was going to receive the award, but he didn’t know, so they asked whether I could get a letter from one of the children we had helped,” Fiesser says. “I was really proud of Bukayo, I think the way he did it was really special. He stood there so strongly for all these children around the world that nobody sees and nobody hears. He gave them a voice. He took the attention away from himself and put it into action. That’s how I know Bukayo. It’s never about him, it’s always about the people we help. He’s incredible.”
Saka, who donated more than 1,000 school uniforms to children in his home borough of Ealing in west London last year to help with the cost of living crisis, is understood to have heard about BigShoe from Antonio Rüdiger after the Real Madrid and Germany defender told him about some of the work he had done with the organisation in Africa. It has also worked with Philipp Lahm and Mesut Özil in the past. Fiesser says Saka and his family have taken a particularly close interest in which projects he supports.
“When we had 150 life-changing surgeries taking place in Nigeria, he would message me asking to see pictures. He wanted to know what was happening and whether everybody was safe. He always asks whether the team has returned safely. I don’t know how he manages to find the time, but he does. His family are very similar. They genuinely want to make a big impact and provide meaningful help. I wouldn’t describe Bukayo as simply a donor to BigShoe. He’s more like a member of the BigShoe team. I know that he stands behind us.”
BigShoe was established by four friends in 2006 after the World Cup. As part of its latest projects in Rwanda and Nigeria, about 3,000 people had eye examinations and were provided with glasses if required. “Giving a child a pair of glasses can change their life,” Fiesser says. “We also help entire families. If a father can’t see properly, he might not be able to work or read. That affects the whole family.”
BigShoe recently renovated a school in Rwanda and provided clean drinking water through a water filtration system. It has also built a library and provided private changing facilities for girls. “Once a month, some girls miss school because they don’t have suitable facilities or somewhere private to change,” says Fiesser. “We built facilities so they can continue attending school and have a quiet, private area.”
Saka’s hectic playing schedule means he has yet to make a visit but his family have been on the ground in Rwanda and he was heavily involved in funding earthquake relief projects in Morocco and Turkey. “We provided container homes for people affected by the earthquakes,” says Fiesser. “I knew I could count on him. It’s always important to Bukayo that we make a big impact. He doesn’t want money to be wasted. When I present a project to him, he wants to understand it properly. He needs to know exactly what we’re doing before he makes a decision. He’s a 100% person. Whatever he does, he gives it everything.”
Saka’s mother, Adenike, is believed to be a driving force behind her son’s charitable work, with Fiesser describing her as “one of the most amazing women I’ve met”. Plans are being made for the next projects, which include providing health insurance to families in Nigeria and food packages for children in Rwanda over Christmas.
“He doesn’t just want to give someone food,” Fiesser says. “Of course, food is important, and we’re providing that too, but he wants to change lives. You can help someone, but if the help doesn’t last, then it hasn’t achieved what you really wanted. If we all work together, it doesn’t matter which team we’re supporting or which country we’re helping. We’re all part of one world.”
digest_he: חלוץ ארסנל, בוקאיו סאקה, זכה בפרס סוקרטס בטקס כדור הזהב בלונדון בזכות פעילותו ההומניטרית והחברתית. ולרי פיסר, נשיאת ארגון הצדקה BigShoe, סיפרה על פנייתו המפתיעה של סאקה ב-2022, שבה ביקש לסייע בפרויקטים בניגריה ומאז הפך לחלק בלתי נפרד מפעילות הארגון. הארגון, שהוקם ב-2006, סייע באלפי ניתוחים, בדיקות ראייה, שיפוץ בתי ספר ואספקת מי שתייה נקיים באפריקה, כמו גם בסיוע לנפגעי רעידות אדמה בטורקיה ובמורוקו. סאקה, אשר תרם אלפי מדי לימוד לילדים בלונדון ומעורב אישית בפרטי הפרויקטים יחד עם משפחתו, מדגיש תמיד את הרצון לשנות חיים מהיסוד ולהעניק עזרה משמעותית ומתמשכת לנזקקים ברחבי העולם.
